I'll start with `PR.diff`, then read the new source around each hunk and report only defects in the changed code.The diff is large. I'll map the hunks and focus on the hook and script changes where logic bugs are likely.The change removes Maestro. I'll check the remaining router, settings, and cleanup script for broken references and unsafe writes.The Maestro removal itself is consistent. The new settings migration script is the part that can corrupt live hook policy or miss the file it is supposed to edit.

`scripts/settings/remove-maestro-registrations.mjs` rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` in place. `writeFileSync` truncates that file before the new JSON is fully written, and a failed write does not restore the `.bak-maestro` copy. The sibling script `capture-active-registrations.mjs` already writes this same file by temp file plus rename so a crash cannot leave Claude with a partial settings file. A truncated settings file does not load, so every hook stays off until someone copies the backup back by hand.

The same script also resolves the target path incorrectly. `node remove-maestro-registrations.mjs --apply` treats `--apply` as the filename, and with no path argument it uses `USERPROFILE` only. When that variable is unset the path is the literal `undefined/.claude/settings.json`, so the dead `maestro-*.mjs` and `session-start-recovery.mjs` registrations are left in place.

Claude then starts with no hook config, so the rest of the harness fails open until the backup is copied back by hand. Write to a temp file in the same directory and rename it over the target, and skip the rewrite when nothing was removed."},{"file":"scripts/settings/remove-maestro-registrations.mjs","line":2,"severity":"minor","title":"Settings path ignores --apply and non-Windows home","body":"The file path is process.argv[2], so `node remove-maestro-registrations.mjs --apply` tries to read a file named --apply and never edits the real settings. The default is USERPROFILE plus '/.claude/settings.json'; when USERPROFILE is unset that string is 'undefined/.claude/settings.json', so macOS, Linux, and CI do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json and the deleted hook commands stay registered. Take the first argument that does not start with --, and default to homedir() joined with '.claude/settings.json'."]}
